html:
This territory is the homeland of the Federated Indians of Graton Rancheria, the tribe formed by the Coast Miwok of Marin and southern Sonoma counties and the Southern Pomo of the Santa Rosa area, north of San Francisco Bay.

These peoples lived in many small villages by the bay, the coast and the valleys, gathering acorns, fishing and collecting shellfish. In 1579 Francis Drake landed on this coast and met Coast Miwok people. Spanish missions at San Rafael and Sonoma in the 1810s and 1820s took in many of them, and Mexican ranches and the Gold Rush years followed.

In 1920 the government bought a small rancheria near Graton for landless Native families. Under the termination policy the United States ended its recognition of the rancheria in 1966. The tribe won it back by an act of Congress in 2000.
sum: This territory is the homeland of the Federated Indians of Graton Rancheria, the tribe formed by the Coast Miwok of Marin and southern Sonoma counties and the Southern Pomo of the Santa Rosa area, north of San Francisco Bay.
